sentences.text: The petitioner is the accused in C.C.No.257 of 2003 (L.P.No.131 of 2013) on the file of the Court of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class-I, Kattappana, which in turn has originated from Crime No.392 of 1999 registered by the Kattappana Police Station, Idukki, alleging the commission offences punishable under Section 419, 420 and 471 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class-I, Kattappana
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The case against the petitioner was split up and the Court of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class-I, Kattappana ('Trial Court', in short) proceeded with the trial as against the 1st accused.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class-I, Kattappana
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: By Annexure A2 judgment, the Trial Court acquitted the 1st accused.
Subsequently, the petitioner got himself enlarged on bail and the case against the petitioner has been numbered again as C.C.No.257 of 2003.

The petitioner has filed this Criminal Miscellaneous Case on the assertion that, in view of Annexure A2 judgment passed in favour of the 1st accused, the substratum of the prosecution case has been lost.
Therefore, even if the petitioner withstands the trial, it is not going to lead to his conviction.
Hence, the proceedings against the petitioner may be quashed.
4. The essence of the prosecution case is that, the defacto complainant (CW1) had sold his vehicle bearing Reg.No.KL-5-F-7277 to the 2nd accused along with the liability of the finance company.

However, as per the directions of the 2nd accused, the 1st accused committed impersonation by Abdul Aziz,S/O Aliyar Meeran vs State Of Kerala on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111873067/
2 pretending to be one Joy and got an agreement executed, and cheated the finance company by not paying the amount due to it.
5.

entities.text: Aliyar Meeran vs State Of Kerala
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
Admittedly, the case against the petitioner was split up and the Trial Court proceeded with the trial as against the 1st accused.
By Annexure A2 judgment, the Trial Court found that CW1 had specifically testified that he was not sure that the signature on Ext.P2 was that of the 1 st accused or of the person named Joy.
He also deposed that the police had not produced the accused before him and had not identified them.
The owner of the premises from where the vehicle was seized also did not testify in tune with the prosecution case.

In view of the lacuna in the prosecution case, the Trial Court came to a conclusion that the prosecution had failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the accused persons had committed the above offences.
Thus, the Trial Court has acquitted the 1st accused.

7. In Moosa v. Sub Inspector of Police [2006 (1) KLT 552], a Full Bench of this Court has held that in a case where the very substratum of the case is lost by the acquittal of the co-accused, the inherent power of this Court can be 2026:KER:28868 CRL.MC NO. 8079 OF 2024 exercised to quash the proceedings against the other accused persons.

entities.text: Moosa v. Sub Inspector of Police [2006 (1) KLT 552]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The same view has been repeatedly reiterated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court and this Court in a catena of precedents.
8. I have carefully analysed the allegations in Annexure A1 final report and the findings in Annexure A2 judgment.

In light of the specific findings in Annexure A2 judgment that the prosecution had failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the 1st accused had committed the above offences, I am satisfied that the substratum of the prosecution case has been lost.
Therefore, even if the petitioner withstands the trial, it is not going to lead to his conviction.
It would be a sheer waste of judicial time to conduct the trial all over again against the petitioner.
Thus, I am satisfied that this is a fit case to exercise the inherent powers of this Court under Section 528 of the Bharathiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.

In the aforesaid circumstances, I allow the Crl.M.C.,
by quashing Annexure A1 final report and all further proceedings in C.C.No.257 of 2003 (L.P.No.131 of 2013) of the Trial Court, as against the petitioner.
